In this example, the left ear's unmasked threshold is fifty decibels.
The true threshold, found with the plateau method, is seventy dB HL.
With too little noise, the other ear still hears the tone.
On the plateau, the threshold holds as noise rises; it is true.
Too much noise crosses to the test ear and raises the threshold.
